Hi Laura,

Thanks again for the demo last week. Procurement here — we had one follow-up from our legal team about the Private Deployment addendum (MSA exhibit). Specifically:

- We need clarity on the evidence you’ll provide to prove "operator capability" at time of handoff (checklist items, witness presence, and whether an independent witness is required).
- Who is the authorized signer for the addendum on Redwood's side (we need the Docusign envelope to match the person on the MSA signature block)?
- Can Redwood accept a limited audit window (three business days) with pre-specified success criteria rather than ongoing audit rights?

Can you confirm what artifacts you’ll provide (snapshots, logs, operator runbooks) and whether these can be delivered under an escrow-like deposit for the MSA exhibit? Attaching our procurement checklist as reference.

Thanks,
Sanjay Rao
Medicore — Sr. Procurement Manager

Sanjay — thanks for the clarity. Looping in Karthik (contracts) and will pull Legal if needed. High-level answers below; detailed redlines and a proposal will follow by end of day tomorrow.

- Operator proof: we can provide a time-bound witness session (onsite or remote) plus a sealed forensic snapshot and a verification checklist showing operator-runbook execution (hash + timestamp).
- Authorized signer: Redwood signs operational exhibits via the Head of Legal or an authorized contracts designee. We’ll confirm the exact name in the DocuSign envelope — happy to put the title on the signature block if that helps.
- Audit window: we’re open to a short, pre-scheduled audit window (3 business days) with pass/fail criteria, but need to preserve limited forensic access for incident investigations for a defined retention period.

I’ll attach our suggested Exhibit B draft and the witnessing checklist. Please let us know if Medicore requires an independent third-party witness or if Redwood’s internal witness plus attestation is sufficient.

Next steps: I’ll share a marked-up exhibit and suggested DocuSign envelope fields tomorrow.

Thanks Laura — quick contract notes from my side (first pass):

1) Language: replace "escrow-like deposit" with "time-limited custodial snapshot deposit" to avoid implying a third-party escrow unless Medicore explicitly requests and funds it.
2) Operator capability: propose a concrete acceptance checklist (attach) that covers 10 items (connectivity, KV cache restore, sample inference, syslog export, account separation tests). Pass = all items validated within the audit window.
3) Witnessing: we can offer Redwood-attested witnessing by an authorized witness (signed attestation). If Medicore requires a third-party witness, we will accept but it will be a procurement/redline that may add costs.
4) Signer identity: include a DocuSign envelope where the signer name and title are explicit; Redwood will provide the signer name at time of sending (Head of Legal or Contracts Director).
5) Audit rights: limit to scheduled windows and an exception for good-faith incident response (retain logs for 180 days) — proposed wording attached as an annotated redline.

Attachments: Proposed_Exhibit_Witnessing.docx (contains the checklist and the suggested acceptance criteria table).

If Medicore agrees in principle to the checklist model, Legal can prepare a tight exhibit that avoids open-ended audit language.

— Karthik
Sr. Contracts Counsel, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: Proposed_Exhibit_Witnessing.docx (docx)]

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Sanjay Rao <sanjay@medicore.com>
Date: Thu, 21 May 2026 09:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Follow up — VPC operator proof & signer identity for on-prem addendum

Sanjay, Karthik — legal had a quick look at Karthik's proposed checklist and redlines. A few items we think are important to lock down in the exhibit:

- Acceptance criteria must be objective (e.g., SHA-256 hash matches for snapshot, successful inference of test vector X within <200ms). Subjective language like "satisfactory" will create friction at sign-off.
- For witness attestation, Redwood can provide an officer-signed attestation and a recorded remote witness session. We will include an option for third-party witnessing as a paid add-on.
- Retention and forensic access: propose 180 days of log retention; forensic access limited to 30 days post-audit or 180 days post-incident with documented cause.
- DocuSign: we’ll add a signature block template clause: "Authorized Redwood Signer: Name, Title, Email — to be populated at execution." This avoids re-opening negotiation over signatory authority.
- Liability carveouts: if Medicore requires long-term custody or third-party escrow, we need to tie that to a written exhibit and separate SOW.

I attached an annotated PDF with inline suggestions. If Medicore can confirm third-party witness requirement now, Legal will draft the limited-scope witness addendum and a cost appendix. Otherwise we’ll ship the exhibit with Redwood-attested witnessing and the checklist.

Marissa Cole
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: Signed_Redlines_annotated.pdf (pdf)]
